newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Bondi Beach to be partly fenced off for Christmas.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Bondi Beach to be partly fenced off for Christmas.

text.p: Australia's Bondi Beach will be partly fenced off on Christmas Day, alcohol will be restricted to a third of the beach, and revellers will have to buy admission tickets in an attempt to avoid a repeat of last year's riot.
Police surveillance cameras will also be installed along the beach and nearby roads, which will be closed to traffic.

The New South Wales state government and local Waverley Council on Thursday announced "Sunsplashed" -- an organised, ticketed Christmas party for Bondi -- in an attempt to restore the beach's tarnished image.

"In light of revellers' behaviour in recent years, alcohol consumption will be restricted to the Sunsplashed enclosure, which will include the Bondi Pavilion, promenade, and ... the middle third of the beach to the waters edge," the government and council said in a joint statement.

"This fenced off beach area is also a strict no glass area, with ticket purchasers being given a commemorative acrylic glass to drink out of for the day. The glass includes a leash to hang it around the neck of the party goer."
Australian police in riot gear clashed with hundreds of Christmas revellers last year as drunken rioting crowds attacked a bus and cars at Sydney's famous beach.
The annual Bondi Beach Christmas Day party attracts around 20,000 people, many of them foreigners.

Ten thousand A$10 tickets are now on sale for this year's Christmas Day party, which will also include a food and entertainment festival. Ticket holders will also be given free phone cards worth A$4 each to phone home from 50 special telephone lines set up in the pavilion.
Organisers said they hoped this year's festivities will restore Bondi's image, tarnished by last year's riot and the bashing murder in September of a British man.
"It's going to be 100 percent better than last year," said Waverley councillor Peter Moscatt.
"We have accepted we can't enforce (alcohol) prohibition on the day and recognised there has to be a designated area where it can be consumed and controlled," Moscatt said.
"Bondi people don't mind people coming to Bondi. They want them to come and if they use the facilities they need to follow the rules. And that means no booze, no glass and no aggro."
